title: 1981 AHSME Problem 28
statement: Consider the set of all equations \(x^3+a_2x^2+a_1x+a_0=0,\) where \(a_2,\) \(a_1,\) \(a_0\) are real constants and \(|a_i|\le2\) for \(i=0,\) \(1,\) \(2.\) Let \(r\) be the largest positive real number which satisfies at least one of these equations. Then

solutions.text:
Write an allowed polynomial as \(g.\) For \(x\ge0,\) \[ \begin{aligned} g(x)&=x^3+a_2x^2\\ &\quad+a_1x+a_0\\ &\ge f(x), \end{aligned} \] where \(f(x)=x^3-2x^2-2x-2.\) Thus no positive root can exceed the largest root \(\rho\) of \(f.\) Taking \(a_2=a_1=a_0=-2\) gives \(g=f,\) so \(\rho\) itself is attained. Since \[ \begin{gathered} f\left(\frac52\right)=-\frac{31}{8}\lt0,\\ f(3)=1\gt0, \end{gathered} \] we have \(\frac{5}{2}\lt\rho\lt3.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: For positive \(x,\) the coefficients that push a root farthest right take their lower bounds
